principles: Only fix measurable token overhead; do not optimize arbitrary prompt prose.
Preserve Lattice lifecycle correctness, reviewer independence, and signed evidence semantics before reducing prompt size.
Keep changes host-neutral: local CLI behavior and managed assets may change, Authority Server receipt semantics may not.
Make reductions measurable through before/after byte or approximate token evidence.
Default command outputs must remain backward compatible; slim behavior must be explicit opt-in.
drivers: Large repeated agent prompt snapshots are the dominant documented token-cost source.
Fresh-context fence and flow-fact/process-gate text are load-bearing and must survive any slimming.
Users need a visible measurable reduction, not just internal cleanup.
B-bfb5 is high-risk because it touches prompt and lifecycle-adjacent surfaces.

options.name: A: Minimal measured prompt slimming plus opt-in slim read outputs
pros: Directly targets the documented repeated snapshot cost.
Preserves default command behavior and signed artifact semantics.
Can be verified with mechanical size and prompt-safety smoke tests.
Keeps Authority/handoff semantics out of scope.
cons: Requires careful template editing and safety assertions for every affected prompt.
Billing savings remain an estimate if provider prompt cache behavior is unknown.

options.name: B: Only add slim story_get/checklist_get output
pros: Default compatibility is easy to preserve.
cons: Leaves the dominant repeated prompt snapshot cost unresolved.
Would not satisfy the audit document main finding or user expectation.

options.name: C: Global prompt architecture rewrite
pros: Could create a cleaner long-term generated prompt system.
May eliminate more drift classes later.
cons: Too broad for the current correctness-focused story.
Higher risk of changing reviewer behavior or lifecycle gate expectations.
Could mix token optimization with unrelated architecture churn.

chosen: A: Minimal measured prompt slimming plus opt-in slim read outputs
rationale: Option A is the narrowest approach that fixes the real documented token overhead while preserving lifecycle correctness, default compatibility, and Authority boundaries.

preMortem.scenario: Slimmed prompts remove a load-bearing fresh-context or flow-fact instruction.
preMortem.trigger: Template snapshot is replaced without checking required phrases and gate semantics.
preMortem.consequence: Reviewers may self-absolve or miss lifecycle evidence requirements, reducing correctness despite lower token use.
preMortem.mitigation: Add prompt-token-cost smoke assertions that required fresh-context, process-fact, review-run, finding/pass, and Authority boundary phrases remain present in every affected prompt.

preMortem.scenario: Slim output breaks existing story_get/checklist_get callers.
preMortem.trigger: Slim behavior changes default output or removes fields unconditionally.
preMortem.consequence: Existing automation, reviewers, or tests fail or silently lose required context.
preMortem.mitigation: Make slim/fields opt-in only; add default-output compatibility checks before asserting token reduction.

preMortem.trigger: Prompt cache behavior reduces billed savings or char/4 conversion is treated as exact billing.
preMortem.consequence: User receives an overclaim rather than a defensible optimization result.
preMortem.mitigation: Report byte and approximate token deltas as context-load reduction, explicitly retaining prompt-cache billing caveat.

preMortem.scenario: Handoff or Authority material from the audit leaks into implementation scope.
preMortem.trigger: Developer treats Q1 takeover/handoff audit sections as code-change targets.
preMortem.consequence: Story changes authority boundaries, receipt semantics, or merge ownership unrelated to token cost.
preMortem.mitigation: Scope contract excludes handoff authority boundary changes, receipt verification, ownership transfer, merge authority, DONE authority, and Authority Server behavior.
